ACTION: Write the design to `specs/harbour-audio-guide.md`
```markdown
# Harbour Museum Audio Guide

## Intent
A visitor scans a code beside an exhibit and hears a roughly two-minute story
about it, in English or Welsh. The stories are recorded by museum volunteers on
their phones. The guide should feel effortless to visitors, and volunteers must
be able to keep it up to date without help from anyone technical.

## Scale
- 60 exhibits, each with an English and a Welsh story (120 recordings).
- About 10 new exhibits a year, plus occasional re-recordings.
- Each recording is about 2 minutes, captured on whatever phone the volunteer has.

## Goals
- Scan, then hear the story, with no app install and no account for visitors.
- The visitor picks a language once. The guide remembers it for later scans and
  lets them change it at any time.
- A volunteer can add or replace a recording on their own.
- Every recording is cleaned up automatically before it goes live: loudness
  levelled, and silence at the start and end trimmed. Visitors hear stories one
  after another, so the volume should stay steady from one to the next.

## Non-goals
- Written transcripts, maps, tours, or visitor accounts.
- Editing audio in the browser. Volunteers re-record instead.
- Languages other than English and Welsh. The structure shouldn't rule them out,
  but nothing gets built for them.

## Anti-goals (a failure even if it works)
- Visitors on patchy museum Wi-Fi or mobile data waiting a long time, or a story
  failing partway through.
- Welsh treated as second-class: an English-only interface, or English shown
  first by default. *(Assumption, not yet confirmed: the museum is in Wales and
  may fall under the Welsh Language Standards.)*
- Volunteers needing to touch the website code, Git, or audio software.
- A bad upload (silence, the wrong file) going live with no way to notice it or
  roll it back.

## Constraints
- The museum's existing site is static Eleventy, deployed on Netlify. Nothing for
  the guide exists yet.
- Phone recordings come in different formats (m4a/AAC from iPhone, often
  m4a/AAC/AMR/webm from Android) and at very different loudness levels.

## Approaches considered (recording handling)
1. **Play uploads as they are.** Simplest, but loudness varies widely between
   phones and speakers, and visitors hear the stories back to back.
2. **Clean up each upload automatically before it goes live (chosen).** Level the
   loudness and trim the silences. The partner chose this.

## How it works

### Visitor side
- Each exhibit has one code, the same for both languages, pointing to
  `/guide/<exhibit-id>/` on the museum site.
- On the first scan, a bilingual chooser ("Cymraeg / English") is shown, with
  Welsh first. The choice is stored on the device, and later scans go straight to
  the story. A visible toggle on every guide page switches language.
- The guide page shows the exhibit name and a play button. *(Builder's call:
  autoplay is usually blocked by phone browsers, so one tap to play is expected.)*
- If a story isn't recorded yet in the chosen language, say so in that language
  and offer the other language. *(My call.)*

### Volunteer side
- A simple, login-protected upload page: pick an exhibit (or add a new one with
  its English and Welsh names), pick a language, upload the phone file.
- The upload is processed, then the volunteer can listen to the cleaned version
  and press "Publish." The previous version is kept so it can be restored.
- Adding an exhibit also produces a printable code for the label.

### Processing
- Convert to a single web-friendly format, level the loudness to one target,
  and trim silence at the start and end. *(Builder's call: e.g. ffmpeg with
  EBU R128 loudness normalisation to around −16 LUFS, a common target for
  phone speakers.)*
- Reject files that come out nearly silent, or much shorter or longer than
  expected, with a plain-language message to the volunteer.

## Hosting and tools (my call, open to change)
Build on what the museum already has: guide pages on the existing Eleventy/Netlify
site, with volunteer login, upload, processing, and storage handled by Netlify's
add-on services (or an equivalent small hosted service if processing doesn't fit
there). This keeps one site and one bill. The builder should confirm that audio
processing fits within the platform's limits before committing to it.

## Left to the builder
- Exact storage, login, and processing services, within the hosting call above.
- Audio format, bitrate, and loudness target.
- Page design, within the museum site's existing look.
- Exhibit IDs and the code format.
```

This is a project rather than a small change. It needs visitor pages, a volunteer upload area, automatic processing, and somewhere to store the audio. So I've written it up as a full design in `specs/harbour-audio-guide.md`, and a reviewer is reading it now as if they had to build from it. I may come back once with a few questions from that review before I hand the document over.

Two things I filled in myself are marked as my calls in the document. First, it builds on the museum's existing website and its hosting, so you keep one site and one bill. Second, the language chooser puts Welsh first, on the assumption that the museum is in Wales.

One practical snag: this folder isn't set up with version history (Git) yet, so I can't save the design there the way I'd like to. Should I set that up here, or does the website's code live somewhere else I should be working in?
